trials.instruction: Create an original PURE DART library implementation for package aivexus_ascii_slug, Dart SDK >=3.3.0 <4.0.0. Put the implementation in lib/ascii_slug.dart and expose the PUBLIC TOP-LEVEL function String toAsciiSlug(String input). Produce a deterministic ASCII-only slug. ASCII letters A-Z become a-z; ASCII letters a-z and ASCII digits 0-9 are preserved; every contiguous run of all other characters (punctuation, whitespace, underscore, non-ASCII Unicode) acts as exactly one separator '-'. Omit separators at the very start and end. Empty or wholly invalid input yields ''. Preserve the order of letters and digits; never omit their characters. IMPORTANT: The output MUST be constructed from VALID ASCII letters and digits, NOT from the punctuation/separator characters. Use a SINGLE left-to-right stateful traversal conceptually: a string output accumulator plus a pending-separator state. Only emit a pending '-' when the NEXT valid ASCII letter or digit is appended and the output is already nonempty; never emit '-' merely because punctuation was seen. This naturally prevents both leading/trailing and consecutive hyphens. IMPORTANT DART API: String.trim() takes ZERO arguments and cannot strip a specified character. NEVER call trim('-'), trimStart('-'), trimEnd('-'), or any method with incorrect Dart arguments; do NOT rely on trimming hyphens after generation. Do not use a no-op replaceAll('-', '-') or a list that stores discarded input punctuation as output. Do not add runtime dependencies, network, IO, shell, FFI or subprocesses. Examples of required functionality (examples, not prewritten source): '  Hello,   WORLD! Foo  ' => 'hello-world-foo'; 'A___B--C' => 'a-b-c'; 'Mixed123Case' => 'mixed123case'; '123+456' => '123-456'; '!!!' => ''. Write COMPLETE ORIGINAL Dart logic yourself, no stubs or predetermined source code; return exactly the JSON source object required by the generation system.

Create a NEW original, pure-Dart reusable package named aivexus_delta_codec, SDK >=3.3.0 <4.0.0, code at lib/delta_codec.dart and behavioral tests under test/. Implement exactly two public functions: List<int> encodeDeltas(List<int> samples), encoding the first sample unchanged and each later entry as current minus previous; List<int> decodeDeltas(List<int> deltas), reconstructing original sample values. Return fresh lists, never mutate arguments. Empty input gives empty output; negative values must work. No external runtime dependencies, network, IO, shell or FFI. Return only the strict JSON files object specified by the system prompt.
